subject: Economy
title: Union Budget 2025–26: fiscal anchor
facts: Total expenditure BE: ₹50.65 lakh crore; non-borrowing receipts: ₹34.96 lakh crore.
Fiscal deficit BE: 4.4% of GDP; capital expenditure: ₹11.21 lakh crore (3.1% of GDP).
trap: Budget estimates are planned figures, not actual spending.
mains: Explain the growth–fiscal consolidation trade-off. Use capex quality, multiplier effects and debt sustainability.

subject: Economy
title: Union Budget 2026–27: compare like with like
facts: Expenditure BE: ₹53.5 lakh crore; non-debt receipts BE: ₹36.5 lakh crore.
Fiscal deficit BE: 4.3% of GDP; debt-to-GDP BE: 55.6%.
Public capital expenditure proposed at ₹12.2 lakh crore.
trap: Do not compare 2025–26 BE with 2026–27 BE and describe the result as realised growth.
mains: Assess whether capex-led consolidation can crowd in private investment.

subject: Economy
title: New-regime personal income-tax relief
facts: Budget announced no personal income tax up to ₹12 lakh of eligible income under the new regime, excluding special-rate income such as capital gains.
For salaried taxpayers, the stated threshold was ₹12.75 lakh with ₹75,000 standard deduction.
trap: This is not a blanket nil-rate slab up to ₹12 lakh; distinguish slab, deduction and rebate. Historical budget position, not current tax advice.
mains: Evaluate consumption stimulus against revenue foregone and distributional effects.

subject: Agriculture
title: PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana: announcement
facts: Budget proposed a state-partnership programme covering 100 districts with low productivity, moderate crop intensity and below-average credit.
The stated potential reach was 1.7 crore farmers.
trap: Announcement, approval and operational launch have different dates; launch guidelines remain a backfill task.
mains: Design district-specific convergence using credit, irrigation, extension and market access.

subject: Agriculture
title: Pulses self-reliance mission
facts: Six-year mission announced with focus on tur, urad and masoor.
Budget proposed NAFED and NCCF procurement of these pulses over the next four years.
trap: Do not confuse the mission duration with the procurement commitment period.
mains: Discuss procurement credibility, diversification and water-efficient cropping.

subject: Agriculture
title: Kisan Credit Card: proposed subvention ceiling
facts: Budget proposed increasing the loan limit under the Modified Interest Subvention Scheme from ₹3 lakh to ₹5 lakh for KCC loans.
trap: A credit or subvention limit is not a cash grant; verify operational circulars before treating the change as in force.
mains: How can formal farm credit reduce dependence on informal lenders without worsening indebtedness?

subject: Agriculture
title: EEZ and high-seas fisheries framework
facts: Budget proposed a sustainable fisheries framework for India’s EEZ and high seas, with special focus on Andaman & Nicobar and Lakshadweep.
trap: EEZ rights and high-seas freedoms are different legal categories.
mains: Connect marine exports with stock conservation, traceability and fisher safety; add AP coastal examples.

subject: Economy
title: MSME classification: proposed expansion
facts: Budget proposed enhancing investment limits by 2.5 times and turnover limits by 2 times for MSME classification.
trap: The multipliers differ. The notification and effective date must be checked separately.
mains: Evaluate whether threshold revision improves scale without weakening support for small firms.

subject: Science & Technology
title: Nuclear Energy Mission and SMRs
facts: Budget announced ₹20,000 crore for research and development of small modular reactors.
The stated goal was at least five indigenously developed SMRs operational by 2033.
Amendments to nuclear-energy and liability legislation were proposed.
trap: A 2033 target is not an achieved capacity figure; a proposed amendment is not an enacted law.
mains: Discuss nuclear expansion through safety, liability, finance, fuel security and decarbonisation.

subject: Society & Welfare
title: Gig workers: proposed social-security linkage
facts: Budget announced identity cards, e-Shram registration and healthcare under PM Jan Arogya Yojana for online-platform gig workers.
trap: Registration does not establish that every worker has received all benefits.
mains: Balance platform flexibility with portable benefits, occupational safety and grievance redress.

subject: Society & Welfare
title: Schools, broadband and AI education
facts: 50,000 Atal Tinkering Labs proposed in government schools over five years.
BharatNet broadband proposed for all government secondary schools and PHCs in rural areas.
AI-for-education Centre of Excellence announced with ₹500 crore outlay.
trap: These are targets and announcements, not verified completed installations.
mains: Digital access must be paired with teacher capacity, accessible content and learning-outcome measurement.

subject: Environment
title: Jal Jeevan Mission and urban financing
facts: Budget proposed extending Jal Jeevan Mission until 2028.
Urban Challenge Fund announced at ₹1 lakh crore, with ₹10,000 crore proposed for 2025–26.
trap: A multi-year fund corpus differs from the annual allocation and actual releases.
mains: Examine water-service sustainability through source protection, O&M and local fiscal capacity.

subject: Economy
title: National Critical Mineral Mission
facts: Cabinet approved ₹16,300 crore expenditure with expected ₹18,000 crore investment by PSUs and others, totalling ₹34,300 crore over seven years.
Value chain spans exploration, mining, beneficiation, processing and end-of-life recovery.
Overseas assets, stockpiles, recycling and processing parks are included.
trap: ₹34,300 crore is not entirely direct government budgetary expenditure.
mains: Explain why processing capability and recycling matter as much as mineral ownership.

subject: Science & Technology
title: SpaDeX: docking milestone
facts: ISRO’s two SpaDeX satellites docked on 16 January 2025.
The mission demonstrated rendezvous, docking and post-docking control capabilities.
trap: Mission launch was in December 2024; the docking milestone falls within this archive’s period.
mains: Explain relevance to multi-launch missions, orbital infrastructure and future human spaceflight.

subject: Science & Technology
title: SpaDeX: undocking milestone
facts: ISRO reported successful undocking on 13 March 2025 at about 09:20 IST.
Undocking occurred in a 460 km circular orbit with 45° inclination; satellites subsequently operated independently.
trap: Docking and undocking are separate milestones; do not merge their dates.
mains: Distinguish rendezvous, docking, power transfer and undocking as separate capabilities.

subject: Andhra Pradesh
title: AP Budget 2025–26: fiscal snapshot
facts: Total expenditure including debt repayment: ₹3,22,359 crore.
Net expenditure excluding debt repayment: ₹2,97,929 crore.
Fiscal deficit BE: ₹79,927 crore, about 4.4% of GSDP; revenue deficit BE: ₹33,186 crore, about 1.8%.
trap: PRS rounds amounts; news reports may use less-rounded figures. Never mix gross and net expenditure.
mains: Evaluate AP’s fiscal space through revenue mobilisation, committed expenditure and capital-asset quality.

subject: Andhra Pradesh
title: AP GSDP: nominal projection versus real growth
facts: AP’s 2025–26 current-price GSDP projected at about ₹18.3 lakh crore.
The projected 14% increase is over the 2024–25 revised estimate.
trap: Current-price growth is not real economic growth.
mains: Use sectoral diversification, productivity and resilient coastal livelihoods to assess growth quality.

subject: Andhra Pradesh
title: Talliki Vandanam: budget proposal
facts: AP Budget proposed ₹15,000 annually for each school-going child in Classes I–XII from 2025–26.
Budget policy description included both government and private schools.
trap: Budget policy intent is not a substitute for beneficiary eligibility GOs, deductions or payment records.
mains: Assess enrolment incentives alongside attendance, learning outcomes and fiscal sustainability.

subject: Andhra Pradesh
title: Fishing-ban relief: budget commitment
facts: AP Budget proposed increasing fishing-ban financial relief from ₹10,000 to ₹20,000.
trap: A budget commitment does not prove disbursal to every eligible fisher.
mains: How can closed-season compensation align livelihood protection with marine stock recovery?

subject: Andhra Pradesh
title: Amaravati innovation hub: proposal
facts: Budget proposed an Amaravati innovation hub linked with five zonal centres.
Mentoring, emerging-sector skills and technology upgrading were stated functions.
trap: Proposed infrastructure should not be described as operational without follow-up evidence.
mains: Propose a decentralised start-up ecosystem linking universities, districts and local industry.

subject: Environment
title: Forest metrics: distinguish ISFR and FAO
facts: MoEFCC review cites ISFR 2023 forest and tree cover at 25.17% of geographical area: forest 21.76%, tree 3.41%.
FAO Global Forest Resources Assessment 2025 placed India ninth in total forest area and third in annual net forest gain.
trap: Report year, underlying data year and definitions differ; these are not interchangeable forest rankings.
mains: Evaluate green-cover gains using ecological quality, native species, fragmentation and community rights.

subject: Environment
title: Ramsar sites: dated 2025 snapshot
facts: MoEFCC’s 2025 review reported 96 Ramsar sites covering about 1.36 million hectares.
It reported 11 additions during 2025.
trap: This is a 2025 year-end count, NOT a verified November 2026 count.
mains: Explain wise use, catchment management and community participation in wetland conservation.

subject: Environment
title: Indore and Udaipur: Ramsar Wetland Cities
facts: The year-end review identifies Indore and Udaipur as India’s first Ramsar Wetland Cities in January 2025.
Exact announcement day is not established here; the date is month-end indexing only.
trap: Wetland City Accreditation is not the same as declaring the entire city a Ramsar site.
mains: Discuss urban wetlands as flood buffers, biodiversity habitats and water-quality infrastructure.
status: Month verified; day is indexing placeholder

subject: Environment
title: Madhav Tiger Reserve and reserve counts
facts: The 2025 environment review reported 58 tiger reserves and identified Madhav Tiger Reserve in Madhya Pradesh as a new reserve.
trap: 58 is the review’s dated snapshot, not a guaranteed current total.
mains: Link protected-area expansion to corridor continuity, relocation safeguards and coexistence.

subject: Environment
title: International Big Cat Alliance framework
facts: According to MoEFCC’s review, the IBCA framework agreement entered into force on 23 January 2025.
The alliance, launched in 2023, covers seven big-cat species.
trap: Launch in 2023 and framework entry into force in 2025 are separate events.
mains: Assess species-focused international cooperation through science, funding and habitat protection.

subject: Environment
title: Contaminated Sites Rules 2025
facts: MoEFCC review records notification of Environment Protection (Management of Contaminated Sites) Rules, 2025 on 24 July 2025.
The review describes a framework for identification, assessment and remediation.
trap: Operational duties and liability must be studied from the Gazette; the review alone is not a complete legal brief.
mains: Apply polluter-pays and precautionary principles to legacy industrial contamination.

subject: Security
title: Operation Sindoor: essential chronology
facts: Defence Ministry review dates commencement to the intervening night of 6–7 May 2025.
It links the operation to the 22 April 2025 Pahalgam terrorist attack.
trap: Operational claims are the Indian government’s account. Do not present contested casualty or battle-damage figures as independently established.
mains: Analyse deterrence, escalation control, counter-terror diplomacy and civilian protection without tactical speculation.

subject: Security
title: Defence production and exports: FY2024–25
facts: MoD review reports defence production of approximately ₹1.51 lakh crore in FY2024–25.
Defence exports reported at ₹23,622 crore for the same financial year.
trap: Production value and exports are different measures; financial year is not calendar year.
mains: Discuss strategic autonomy through R&D, private-sector participation, procurement reform and export compliance.

subject: Polity & Governance
title: SVAMITVA: distribution and later preparation totals
facts: MoPR review reports 65 lakh property cards distributed on 18 January 2025.
As of 16 December 2025, it reports about 2.76 crore cards prepared and drone flying completed in 3.28 lakh villages.
trap: Prepared, distributed and legally disputed titles are different categories; do not use one as a proxy for another.
mains: Assess drone-based rural property mapping through credit access, dispute resolution and safeguards for excluded residents.

subject: Polity & Governance
title: SabhaSaar and Gram Sabha record-keeping
facts: MoPR’s review highlights an AI-enabled SabhaSaar tool for Gram Sabha record-keeping.
The same review identifies Gram Manchitra as a GIS-based spatial planning platform.
trap: AI transcription support is not a substitute for statutory Gram Sabha procedures or accountable decisions.
mains: Design digital local governance with language access, human validation, privacy and public auditability.

subject: Polity & Governance
title: PESA capacity building: Telugu connection
facts: MoPR review records that Andhra Pradesh and Telangana completed translation of all seven PESA training manuals into Telugu.
trap: Translation of manuals does not itself establish effective devolution or implementation of every PESA protection.
mains: Evaluate the gap between legal Gram Sabha powers and administrative practice in Scheduled Areas.

subject: Polity & Governance
title: Visakhapatnam e-governance declaration
facts: DARPG year-end review records the 28th National e-Governance Conference in Visakhapatnam and adoption of the Visakhapatnam declaration.
trap: The review date is used for indexing; it is not asserted as the conference date.
mains: Use citizen-centric service delivery, interoperability, grievance resolution and accessibility as evaluation criteria.

subject: International Relations
title: India–UK CETA: signing milestone
facts: India and the UK signed CETA on 24 July 2025 after negotiations concluded on 6 May 2025.
PIB signing release describes zero-duty access on 99% of tariff lines, covering nearly all trade value.
trap: Signing, ratification and entry into force are distinct; tariff-line coverage is not the same as trade-value coverage.
mains: Assess opportunities for labour-intensive exports alongside rules of origin, standards compliance and adjustment costs.

subject: International Relations
title: CETA: announced entry-into-force date
facts: PIB’s 17 June 2026 release announced that CETA and the social-security contribution agreement were set to enter into force on 15 July 2026.
It records the companion convention’s signing on 10 February 2026.
trap: This note verifies an advance announcement. Post-15 July implementation notification has not been checked here.
mains: Explain why social-security coordination matters for temporary professional mobility.
status: Official announcement checked; implementation follow-up pending

subject: Economy
title: Export Promotion Mission: architecture
facts: Commerce review describes ₹25,060 crore outlay over FY2025–26 to FY2030–31.
NIRYAT PROTSAHAN focuses on affordable trade finance.
NIRYAT DISHA focuses on non-financial enablers such as quality compliance, branding and logistics.
trap: Do not reverse the two sub-schemes; approved outlay is not expenditure already incurred.
mains: How can export policy combine working-capital access with quality and logistics competitiveness?

subject: Economy
title: Exports: FY2024–25 source snapshot
facts: Commerce review reports combined merchandise and services exports of US$825.25 billion in FY2024–25.
Services exports: US$387.54 billion; merchandise exports: US$437.70 billion (rounding applies).
trap: Historical release figures may be revised; do not label them the latest FY2025–26 totals.
mains: Explain services-led export resilience and the need to widen manufacturing competitiveness.

subject: Science & Technology
title: Biopharma SHAKTI: Budget 2026 proposal
facts: Budget announced ₹10,000 crore over five years for Biopharma SHAKTI.
It proposed three new NIPERs, upgrades to seven existing NIPERs and over 1,000 accredited clinical-trial sites.
trap: Proposed institutions and accredited sites are not all operational simply because the budget names them.
mains: Connect biologics capacity to regulation, trial ethics, affordability and skilled human resources.

subject: Science & Technology
title: India Semiconductor Mission 2.0
facts: Budget proposed ISM 2.0 for equipment and materials, full-stack Indian IP, supply chains and industry-led research and training.
Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme outlay proposed to increase to ₹40,000 crore.
trap: Distinguish chip design, fabrication, packaging and equipment ecosystems; the two initiatives are not identical.
mains: Evaluate semiconductor resilience beyond subsidy totals: skills, water, power, IP and downstream demand.

subject: Andhra Pradesh
title: Rare Earth Corridors: AP in the Union Budget
facts: Dedicated Rare Earth Corridors proposed for Odisha, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.
The stated scope includes mining, processing, research and manufacturing.
trap: A budget-listed corridor does not establish that a particular AP mine or processing plant has received all clearances.
mains: Assess coastal mineral development through value addition, radiation safety where relevant, ecology and local livelihoods.

subject: Environment
title: CCUS: Budget 2026 funding proposal
facts: Union Budget announced ₹20,000 crore over five years for Carbon Capture, Utilization and Storage technologies.
trap: Capture, utilisation and permanent geological storage are not equivalent climate outcomes.
mains: Evaluate CCUS through lifecycle emissions, permanence, energy penalty, cost and hard-to-abate sector needs.

subject: Economy
title: SME Growth Fund and legacy industrial clusters
facts: Budget proposed ₹10,000 crore SME Growth Fund.
A separate proposal covers revival of 200 legacy industrial clusters.
Additional ₹2,000 crore proposed for the Self-Reliant India Fund.
trap: Do not aggregate distinct funds as if they were one scheme with common eligibility.
mains: Compare equity support with credit guarantees and common infrastructure as MSME policy tools.

subject: Andhra Pradesh
title: AP Budget 2026–27: selected allocations
facts: PRS analysis records ₹6,105 crore for the Polavaram dam project and ₹6,000 crore for Amaravati Capital City Development.
It lists ₹6,600 crore for Annadata Sukhibhava and ₹1,420 crore for Stree Shakti free bus travel for women.
trap: Month-end indexing date only: exact presentation day not checked in this note. Allocations do not demonstrate project completion or beneficiary payment.
mains: Compare welfare and infrastructure spending using outcomes, execution capacity and recurrent fiscal liabilities.
status: PRS table checked; event day pending

subject: Polity & Governance
title: Advance tax devolution: national and AP figures
facts: Union released ₹1,09,019 crore as the regular November tax-devolution instalment on 5 November instead of the normal 10 November date.
The PIB state-wise table lists ₹4,597 crore for Andhra Pradesh and ₹2,370 crore for Telangana.
trap: This was an advance of the regular instalment, not a newly announced additional grant or revised devolution formula.
mains: Separate predictability of state cash flows from the constitutional and Finance Commission framework for tax sharing.

subject: Polity & Governance
title: Waqf Amendment Act 2025: assent milestone
facts: Gazette text records Presidential assent on 5 April 2025, Act No.14 of 2025.
The Act amended the Waqf Act, 1995 and included provisions for a portal/database and filing property details.
trap: Assent is not automatically commencement; later Supreme Court orders and operational deadlines must be checked before a current-law answer.
mains: Frame a balanced answer around religious freedom, property administration, due process and judicial review.
status: Historical Act checked; current litigation status pending
